claims.text: The initial material is an unmodified elemental Cr coating on a zirconium-alloy fuel-cladding substrate.
Nitrogen ion implantation at approximately 80 keV can localize the peak nitrogen concentration near the Cr/Zr interface.
Implanted nitrogen will induce in-situ formation of CrN precipitates near the Cr/Zr interface.
The treatment can produce a uniform near-interface CrN diffusion barrier.
Finely dispersed CrN precipitates hinder the atomic mobility of Cr and Zr.
Reduced Cr and Zr atomic mobility will suppress elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Approximately 350°C subcritical water represents the normal-operation condition relevant to the hypothesis.
Approximately 1200°C steam for up to one hour represents an accident-relevant exposure condition.
An unmodified elemental Cr coating on zirconium alloy is prone to pronounced Cr–Zr interdiffusion in high-temperature steam.
After 1200°C steam exposure, nitrogen-implanted coatings will have a significantly thinner or absent Cr–Zr interdiffusion zone relative to unmodified coatings.
The nitrogen-implanted coating will retain coating integrity and corrosion resistance during extended exposure to approximately 350°C subcritical water.
CrN and Cr/CrN coatings are prior protective-coating concepts for zirconium-alloy accident-tolerant fuel cladding.
Uniform nitrogen implantation over curved cladding surfaces and precise control of the implantation depth profile require optimization.
EDS elemental mapping can characterize interfacial diffusion profiles and interdiffusion-zone thickness.
Cross-sectional TEM can determine the presence, uniformity, and morphology of near-interface CrN precipitates.
Three-point bending and adhesion measurements can assess post-exposure coating mechanical integrity.
Failure to achieve a statistically significant reduction in interdiffusion-zone thickness, or compromised integrity or coating failure under either exposure condition, falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention places the nitrogen peak near the buried Cr/Zr interface, whereas the structural mediator is described as a 'near-surface region' within the Cr coating; unless 'near-surface' is intended to mean the substrate-facing interface, these locations are inconsistent.
